It is also referred to as "Tamaru-hime Falls" in alternate kanji<ref name="chinoshishigekan">‘Chino City History: Modern and Folklore,’ pp. 1069–1070.</ref><ref>‘Chino City History: Supplement Natural History,’ p. 33.</ref>. The falls are designated as a cultural property by Chino City.

== Geography ==
'''Tamaru-hime Falls''' is located east of Chino City's central area, at the foot of [[Mount Oizumi]], along the [[Yanagawa (Nagano)|Yanagawa River]]. From the summit of Mount Oizumi, one can see {{ill|Mount Fuji|abstract|Q39231|af|Foedji|am|ፉጂ ተራራ|an|Mont Fuji|ang|Fucgi Beorg|ar|جبل فوجي|arz|جبل فوجى|as|মাউণ্ট ফুজি|ast|Monte Fuji|az|Fuci|azb|فوجی‌یاما|ba|Фудзияма|ban|Gunung Fuji|bcl|Bukid Fuji|be|Фудзіяма|be_x_old|Фудзіяма|bew|Gunung Puji|bg|Фуджи|bn|ফুজি পর্বত|br|Menez Fuji|bs|Fuji|btm|Gunung Fujiama|ca|Mont Fuji|ceb|Fujiyama|ckb|چیای فوجی|cs|Fudži|cy|Mynydd Fuji|da|Fuji|de|Fuji (Vulkan)|dv|ފުޖީ ފަރުބަދަ|el|Φούτζι|eo|Monto Fuĵi|es|Monte Fuji|et|Fuji|eu|Fuji mendia|fa|کوه فوجی|fi|Fuji (vuori)|fr|Mont Fuji|frr|Fuji|ga|Sliabh Fuji|gan|富士山|gl|Monte Fuji|gn|Hujisã|hak|Fuji-sân|he|הר פוג'י|hi|फ़ूजीयामा|hr|Fuji|hu|Fudzsi|hy|Ֆուձիյամա|ia|Monte Fuji|iba|Gunung Fuji|id|Gunung Fuji|ie|Monte Fuji|io|Fujiyama|is|Fuji|it|Fuji (monte)|ja|富士山|jv|Gunung Fuji|ka|ფუძიამა|ki|Kĩrĩma gĩa Bunji|kk|Фудзияма|km|ភ្នំហ្វឹជី|kn|ಮೌಂಟ್ ಫುಜಿ|ko|후지산|ku|Çiyayê Fuji|ky|Фужи тоосу|la|Mons Fuji|lld|Mont Fuji|lmo|Fuji|lo|ພູເຂົາຟູຈິ|lt|Fudžijama|lv|Fudzi|mk|Фуџи|ml|ഫുജി പർവ്വതം|mn|Фүжи уул|mr|माउंट फुजी|ms|Gunung Fuji|mt|Fuji|my|ဖူဂျီတောင်|mzn|فوجی یاما|ne|फुजी हिमाल|nl|Fuji (vulkaan)|nn|Fuji-fjellet|no|Fuji-san|oc|Mont Fuji|or|ଫୁଜି ପର୍ବତ|os|Фудзиямæ|pa|ਮਾਊਂਟ ਫੂਜੀ|pam|Bunduk Fuji|pl|Fudżi|pms|Mont Fuji|pnb|فیوجی|pt|Monte Fuji|ro|Fuji|ru|Фудзияма|sat|ᱢᱟᱣᱩᱱᱴ ᱯᱷᱩᱡᱤ|sc|Monte Fuji|scn|Fujiama|sco|Moont Fuji|sh|Fuji|si|ෆූජි කන්ද|simple|Mount Fuji|sk|Fudžisan|sl|Fudži|so|Buurka Jabaan Fuji|sq|Fuxhi|sr|Fudži|su|Gunung Fuji|sv|Fuji|sw|Mlima Fuji|szl|Fuji (berg)|szy|Bu-s buyu’|ta|பூஜி மலை|te|ఫ్యూజీ పర్వతం|th|ภูเขาฟูจิ|tl|Bundok Fuji|tok|nena Pusi|tr|Fuji Dağı|tt|Фудзияма|uk|Фудзі (гора)|ur|کوہ فیوجی|uz|Fudziyama|vi|Phú Sĩ|war|Bukid Fuji|wuu|富士山|xmf|ფუძიამა|zh|富士山|zh_classical|富士山|zh_min_nan|Hù-sū-san|zh_yue|富士山|qid=Q39231|lt=Mount Fuji}} to the left of [[:en:Mount Yatsugatake|Mount Yatsugatake]], with the falls visible below<ref name="choson_3351">‘Nagano Prefectural Town and Village Records: Chuo and Minami-Shin Regions,’ p. 3351.</ref>. The falls have an initial drop of 9 meters in height and width, followed by a right-angle turn with a 3-meter height and 1-meter width<ref name="taki100_120" />. The records describe the water flow as resembling a beaded curtain, producing a sound akin to a harp in the wind. name="choson_3351" />. Downstream, the Yanakage and Nagare Bridges span the falls<ref name="kahimap">{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.chino.lg.jp/uploaded/attachment/3786.pdf |title=Tamaru-hime Literature and Nature Park Monument Map |publisher=Tamaru-hime Literature and Nature Park Creation Committee |accessdate=2020-01-03 }}</ref>, while the Tamaru-hime Bridge of [[Nagano Prefectural Route 17]] crosses the valley<ref>Geospatial Information Authority of Japan "[http://watchizu.gsi.go.jp/watchizu.html?longitude=138.21555558329&latitude=35.993490818409 Watchizu]" (Accessed May 26, 2012).</ref>.

Next to the falls is '''Tamaru-hime Shrine'''<ref name="taki100_120" />, dedicated to {{ill|Tamaru-hime|ja|多満留姫|qid=Q56347882|lt=Tamaru-hime}} (daughter of {{ill|Takeminakata|es|Takeminakata|hu|Takeminakata|id|Takeminakata|it|Takeminakata|ja|タケミナカタ|mni|ꯇꯀꯦꯃꯤꯅꯀꯇ|pl|Takeminakata|zh|建御名方神|qid=Q9150391|lt=Takeminakata}}, the deity of {{ill|Suwa-taisha|abstract|Q218813|de|Suwa-Taisha|es|Suwa taisha|eu|Suwa taisha|fa|زیارتگاه بزرگ سووا|fr|Suwa-taisha|hu|Szuva templom|id|Kuil Suwa|it|Santuario di Suwa (Sohonsha)|ja|諏訪大社|ko|스와 대사|lt|Suvos maldykla|pl|Suwa Taisha|ru|Сува-тайся|simple|Suwa-taisha|tr|Suwa-taisha|zh|諏訪大社|qid=Q218813|lt=Suwa taisha}})<ref>‘Japanese Historical Place Names: Volume 20, Nagano Prefecture,’ p. 358.</ref>. While the shrine's founding date is unknown, it is documented to have existed over 750 years ago<ref name="taki100_120" />.

Chino City designated Tamaru-hime Falls as a cultural property on [[July 29, 1988]] (Showa 63)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.chino.lg.jp/soshiki/bunkazai/1665.html |title=City Designated Cultural Properties |publisher=Chino City |date=2018-12-03 |accessdate=2020-01-03 }}</ref>. The surrounding area, known as '''Tamaru-hime Literature and Nature Park''', is managed by a committee from local districts that maintains and hosts events<ref name="hp">{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.chino.lg.jp/soshiki/shogaigakushu/851.html |title=Tamaru-hime Literature and Nature Park |publisher=Chino City |date=2019-12-20 |accessdate=2020-01-03 }}</ref>. Various monuments inscribed with poems and haiku by notable figures, such as [[:en:Matsuo Basho|Matsuo Basho]], are found in the area, along with submission boxes for original works<ref name="kahimap" />. The park's mascot is '''Tamaru-hime-chan''', depicted sitting on a scroll in the falls' basin<ref name="hp" />. In 2014, to commemorate the park's 10th anniversary, a new mascot named '''Shion''' (紫音) was introduced, designed by local high school students<ref name="hp" /><ref>{{Cite news |url=http://www.nagano-np.co.jp/modules/news/article.php?storyid=31134 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140517123128/http://www.nagano-np.co.jp/modules/news/article.php?storyid=31134 |title=Local Charm: Tamaru-hime Character Introduced by Chino Creation Committee to Promote the Falls |newspaper=[[Nagano Daily News]] |publisher=Nagano Newspaper |date=2014-04-18 |archivedate=2014-05-17 |accessdate=2020-01-03 }}</ref>.

== Legends ==
;{{ill|Lending Bowl Legend|ja|椀貸伝説|qid=Q24862355}}
: A legend tells of Tamaru-hime lending bowls to villagers in need. The following summary is derived from ‘{{ill|Q97184907|ja|長野県史|qid=Q97184907}}’:
:: Long ago, a hardworking couple with a harmonious relationship was blessed with a child. Wanting to celebrate but unable to afford sufficient bowls for the guests, they dreamed of Tamaru-hime instructing them to write their needs on paper and drop it into the falls' basin. Upon doing so, the bowls appeared the next morning. After the celebration, the couple cleaned the bowls and returned them. However, a lazy villager, hearing of this, tried the same but kept one bowl, believing it wouldn't be noticed. Since then, Tamaru-hime ceased lending<ref>‘Nagano Prefectural History: Folklore Edition, Volume II (3),’ pp. 589–591.</ref>.
: Another version suggests that broken bowls caused Tamaru-hime to stop lending<ref name="chinoshishigekan" />.

== Access ==
;[[:en:Public Transportation|Public Transportation]]
: A short walk west from Tamaru-hime Shrine leads to Kizandō. Proceeding further brings you to [[Nagano Prefectural Route 188]] at Nakazawa Intersection, near Nakazawa Bus Stop<ref>"[http://www.mapion.co.jp/m/35.9901438_138.2181119_8/v=m5:%E5%A4%9A%E7%95%99%E5%A7%AB%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE/ Mapion Map: Tamaru-hime Shrine]" (Accessed May 31, 2012).</ref>.
